issue_body:
Widgets are being created with blank names and names full of punctuation, which breaks exports.

`POST /widgets` must reject a name that is empty, longer than 64 characters, or contains a character outside letters, digits, space, `_` and `-`. A rejected name returns HTTP 422 with `{"error": {"code": "invalid_name", "message": ...}}`. The message should tell the user what to fix.

plan.summary: Validate widget names on POST /widgets and return an invalid_name error for a rejected name.

approach.description: Add validateWidgetName in internal/api/validate.go checking emptiness, a 64-character maximum and the allowed character set [A-Za-z0-9 _-].
Call validateWidgetName in the POST /widgets handler before CreateWidget and return HTTP 422 with code invalid_name and a message on failure.
Write one message per failed rule, worded for the person who submitted the form.
Document the invalid_name error and the allowed characters in api/openapi.yaml.

verification.test_strategy: Table-driven handler tests in widgets_test.go: each invalid-name shape asserts 422 and the invalid_name code, and a valid name asserts 201.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR. The change is additive; no data migration needs reversing.

acceptance_criteria.statement: POST /widgets with an empty name returns HTTP 422 with error code invalid_name.
POST /widgets with a 65-character name returns HTTP 422 with error code invalid_name.
POST /widgets with the name "gizmo!" returns HTTP 422 with error code invalid_name.
POST /widgets with the name "gizmo-2" returns HTTP 201.
Validation error messages are clear and user-friendly.

risks_and_assumptions: Existing widgets with now-invalid names are left as they are; only creation is validated.

catching_examples.note: ac-name-message-friendly is not concretely verifiable: 'clear and user-friendly' gives no pass/fail condition; require each message to name the failed rule, e.g. 'name must be at most 64 characters'.
ac-name-message-friendly is subjective; an executor cannot decide whether a message qualifies.
The criterion that messages are clear and user-friendly is vague; state what each message must contain.

non_catching_examples.note: No test covers a name of exactly 64 characters, the longest one accepted.
The same name rules should apply to PATCH /widgets/{id}; the plan changes only POST.
api/openapi.yaml should list the invalid_name error with an example message.
ac-name-message-friendly could be checked in the same table-driven test as ac-name-empty-422.
A user-friendly message that echoes the submitted name back should escape it before it is logged.
